                    ### Question
                    A 74-year-old man with a history of encephalomyelitis, ataxia, and nystagmus a new diagnosis of small cell carcinoma of the lung (T2, N1, Mn/a) is admitted to the hospital due to painless loss of vision in his right eye. A full workup reveals optic neuritis and uveitis in the affected eye. Which of the following antibodies is most likely to be present in the serum of the patient?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Anti-Yo
opb. Anti-amphiphysin
opc. Anti-Hu
opd. Anti-Ri
ope. Anti-CV2 (CRMP5)

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In this case, the 74-year-old man with small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is likely to have paraneoplastic neurological syndromes, which are commonly associated with this type of cancer. The presence of optic neuritis and uveitis suggests an autoimmune process, which is consistent with the known associations of certain antibodies in patients with SCLC. Among the options, Anti-Hu antibodies are most commonly linked to small cell lung cancer and are known to be present in patients with paraneoplastic syndromes, particularly those involving neurological symptoms. While Anti-Yo is associated with cerebellar ataxia, it is less common in SCLC. Anti-Ri is linked to uveitis but is also less prevalent in this context. Anti-amphiphysin is associated with myelitis but not specifically with optic neuritis. Anti-CV2 (CRMP-5) is linked to various neurological symptoms but is not specific to SCLC. Therefore, the most likely antibody present in this patient is Anti-Hu, given its strong association with small cell lung cancer and related neurological manifestations.
